newsitem.title: USA: Money managers less defensive on U.S. debt-survey.
newsitem.headline: Money managers less defensive on U.S. debt-survey.

text.p: After shortening their positions in U.S. debt for several weeks in a row, money managers eased their defensive posture somewhat over the past week, said a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Participants remain quite short overall, but they did extend duration, coinciding with the turn in the market," the report said.

In the week ended February 3, duration bogey slipped to 4.15 from 4.16 on an arithmetic basis and dropped to 4.70 from 4.74 on a weighted basis. Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

The survey's bear/bull index rose to 5.21 from 4.86 the prior week on an arithmetic basis. It rose to 4.9 from 4.79 on an asset-weighted basis. A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market. The cash/assets ratio fell to 7.21 percent from 7.53 percent.
Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 8.0 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active rose to 5.67 from 5.50 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
